nativeRange: Native across much of Europe and Asia; common synanthrope in East Asia including Hong Kong; introduced populations elsewhere (e.g. parts of North America).
habitat: Towns, villages, farmland edges, parks, and open woodland edges. Nests in cavities, buildings, and other human structures; often forages on bare or sparsely vegetated ground in flocks.
seasonality: Year-round resident across most of its range, including Hong Kong / coastal South China; not a long-distance migrant.
lookalikes: House Sparrow (Passer domesticus) — gray crown, no black cheek patch
caution: Wild bird — observe without handling or feeding bread; keep distance from nests.
populationEstimate: 215–305 million mature individuals globally (preliminary; may underestimate eastern densities)
populationSource: BirdLife International / IUCN Red List 2025 (Passer montanus; Least Concern; estimate year 2011, data quality poor)
sources: BirdLife DataZone — Eurasian Tree Sparrow factsheet (population 215–305M mature individuals)
